clue.text: Combination seal ultimately lacking

indicators.note: the word for seal goes without its final letter, its ultimate one

parts.note: to seal off a road is to block it

explanation.surface: A sealant made from a mixture of ingredients is missing something at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloc is a combination of nations or parties acting together as one group.

clue.text: Fibrous connective tissues taking little time to rise in layers

indicators.note: the word for layers takes in, or holds, the other piece

parts.note: strata are layers, as of rock

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a little time

explanation.surface: Fibrous tissues slowly building up in layers over a short span.
explanation.definitionFit: Stromata are the supporting frameworks of connective tissue in an organ, a biological term.

clue.text: Wash without audio aid? Get away!

indicators.note: the word for wash is written without the other piece inside it

parts.note: a shampoo is a hair wash
an amp, short for amplifier, helps sound be heard

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a wash can be done with no hearing aid, then tells a person to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is the exclamation used to drive away an animal or person, much like scram.

clue.text: Season has ended — make an appearance, quickly!

parts.note: spring is one of the four seasons
when time is up it has ended

explanation.surface: The season is over, so someone is urged to turn up without delay.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring up is to arise or emerge suddenly, like weeds after rain.

clue.text: Cook might have done so around North China

indicators.note: the cooking word goes around the other letter

parts.note: a cook might have fried something

explanation.surface: A cook may have prepared something in a northern Chinese style.
explanation.walkthrough: China is rhyming slang: china plate means mate. The capital C disguises it as the country.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china (plate) means mate, so a pal or companion.

clue.text: Service craft: Weightless Moth

indicators.note: a ton is a weight, so the moth's name is written less that weight

parts.note: the Mother Shipton is a British moth, named after a legendary Yorkshire prophetess, its wing marking resembling a witch's profile

explanation.surface: A spacecraft service hub with a weightless moth floating inside.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mother Shipton is a day-flying British moth; take away TON, a weight, and the craft remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A mothership is a large vessel that services and supplies smaller craft operating from it.

clue.text: Night-time threats to females (two Brummies nursing new offspring)

indicators.note: the two letters hold the other pieces between them, as if nursing them

parts.note: Brummie is the setter, who would say I, so two of them give I twice
a cub is a young animal, an offspring

explanation.surface: Two Birmingham folk minding a newborn seem a danger to women at night.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's pseudonym stands for I, the setter's own voice; Brummie also means a person from Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi were demons thought to lie with sleeping women at night, so menaces to them.

clue.text: Flag down Cook?

parts.note: feeling down is feeling blue
Peter Cook was the British comedian, partner of Dudley Moore

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a cook might be lowered like a flag.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook is the comedian Peter Cook, not a chef.
explanation.definitionFit: The Blue Peter is the blue-and-white signal flag hoisted when a ship is about to sail.

clue.text: Fasten strip across counter top

indicators.note: the strip lies across, enclosing, the other letter

parts.note: a lath is a thin strip of wood

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Secure a strip of material across the top of a kitchen counter.
explanation.definitionFit: To latch a door or gate is to fasten it with a catch.

clue.text: Navy takes issue when commandeered by Shell staff

indicators.note: the navy group is taken over and held inside the word for shell

parts.note: to peel is to shell, as with peas or prawns

indicators.note: the navy abbreviation takes the issue inside it

parts.note: RN is the Royal Navy
a son is issue, offspring

explanation.surface: A naval dispute after an oil company seizes control, affecting its workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: Shell looks like the oil company but is a verb meaning peel.
explanation.definitionFit: Personnel are the people employed by an organisation, its staff.

clue.text: Rushes to back of queue, showing false emotion

indicators.note: the rushing word joins the back, the end, of the word for queue

parts.note: a crocodile is a line of schoolchildren walking in pairs, a queue
tears means rushes, dashes

explanation.surface: Someone dashes to the end of a line, putting on a show of feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: A crocodile, in British use, is a line of schoolchildren walking two by two.
explanation.definitionFit: Crocodile tears are an insincere display of sorrow, from the myth that crocodiles weep while eating.

clue.text: See 26
Boat at sea in secure area of decomposing matter

indicators.note: the shuffled boat goes in the word for secure

parts.note: to peg is to secure, as a tent

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A boat drifting at sea is tied up in a sheltered spot where things rot.
explanation.definitionFit: A peat bog is wetland where plant material slowly decays into peat.

clue.text: See 8
Roof's berry-smeared — pity

indicators.note: smeared means smudged out of shape, so these letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone is sorry that a roof has been stained with berry juice.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sorry for someone is to feel compassion for them, a phrasal synonym for the verb.

clue.text: Large, in bold: TREASURE

indicators.note: the large letter is put in the word for bold

parts.note: daring means bold, brave
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing

explanation.surface: A typesetting note: print the word TREASURE in large bold type.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure as a term of endearment for a loved one matches darling.

clue.text: Old Greek physician: "Wind precedes indigestion, ultimately"

indicators.note: the wind word comes before the next piece

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: An ancient doctor's diagnosis: wind comes first, then indigestion.
explanation.definitionFit: Galen was the famous second-century Greek medical writer whose works guided medicine for centuries.

clue.text: See 11
Backing down hollow

indicators.note: backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: down is soft fuzz, the nap on cloth

explanation.surface: Backing down into a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: A pan is a hollow or depression in the ground, as in a salt pan.

clue.text: Anatomising includes particular kinds of atom

indicators.note: anatomising means dissecting, so the letters are taken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: Dissecting something reveals which specific atoms it contains.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclide is an atomic species defined by its numbers of protons and neutrons.

clue.text: Rejected member that went unheard as a philosopher

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so these pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a leg is a limb, a member
Eh? is what someone says when something went unheard

explanation.surface: A rejected member of a group whose ideas went unheard, as a thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rejected' turns the whole charade round; 'member' is a limb, not a club member.
explanation.definitionFit: Hegel was the German idealist thinker known for his dialectic.

clue.text: Graphical user interface initially overlapping cross tip

indicators.note: the two pieces overlap, interleaved so that part of the second sits inside the first
initially points to the first letter of each word

parts.note: ratty means cross, irritable

explanation.surface: A computer interface whose design overlaps with a cross-shaped pointer tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlapping' meshes GUI (from 'initially') with RATTY: G, then RAT, then UI, then TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A gratuity is money given for service, a tip.

clue.text: Left the room scratched?

definitions.meaning: to retire is to withdraw to another room or to bed
a horse scratched from a race has withdrawn, been pulled out

explanation.surface: Someone stormed out after being scratched.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses mean withdrawn: from company, and from a race or contest.

clue.text: Naughty kid's fiddle

definitions.meaning: a little ... is a mischievous child

explanation.surface: A mischievous child's violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinker names an impish child and, as a verb, aimless adjusting or meddling.

clue.text: Revolutionary worker drowned in Wear

indicators.note: the worker is submerged inside the word for wear

parts.note: to don is to put on, wear
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A rebel labourer drowned in the River Wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Wear looks like the River Wear in north-east England but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Danton was a leading figure of the French Revolution.

clue.text: Leader's liable to be entertained by relative killer

indicators.note: the word for liable is held inside, entertained as a guest, by the killer

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
apt means liable, inclined

explanation.surface: A leader likely to be welcomed by a murderer in the family.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is the leader of a team or ship's crew.

clue.text: Guardian cuts honeydew fudge for children's home

indicators.note: the newspaper's word cuts into the melon's letters
to fudge is to fake or muddle, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the Guardian refers to itself as us, the paper's we

explanation.surface: The newspaper slices up a melon and makes sweets for a children's institution.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wendy house is a toy playhouse, named after the house built for Wendy in Peter Pan; 'home' suggests an orphanage.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wendy house is a small playhouse for children, a home of their own.

clue.text: No head on Nick's mop

indicators.note: the word for nick is written with its head, its first letter, dropped

parts.note: to swipe is to nick, steal

explanation.surface: Nick's mop has lost its head.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe a floor is to mop it, clean with a cloth.

clue.text: Corrections to banish URL digital cleanser

indicators.note: corrections rework these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Edits made to remove a web address from an electronic cleaning program.
explanation.walkthrough: Digital refers to digits, fingers, not computers.
explanation.definitionFit: A nailbrush cleans fingernails, the digits, so it is a cleanser for them.

clue.text: Inventor's three lives

parts.note: to live is to be, so lives gives the verb be

indicators.note: three tells us the word lives does triple duty: once as a verb, then twice as the wiring abbreviation

parts.note: in electrical wiring live is abbreviated to a single letter

explanation.surface: An inventor's three lifetimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Graham Bell is credited with inventing the telephone.

clue.text: Catch wine circle substituting carbon

indicators.note: the circle letter takes the place of the carbon letter

parts.note: hock is German white wine
C is the chemical symbol for carbon
O is circle-shaped

explanation.surface: Catch a wine circle swapping out carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: A hook is a device to catch fish, or a catch on a door.

clue.text: Chemical secretion more flexible in mobile device?

indicators.note: the bent letters go in the device word

parts.note: a phone is a mobile device

indicators.note: flexible means bendable, so the letters are bent into new order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a chemical is more pliable when inside a mobile.
explanation.definitionFit: A pheromone is a chemical released by an animal to signal others of its species.

clue.text: Hogarth cloistered courtyard erased on right of illuminated print

indicators.note: the remaining letters sit to the right of the lit word

parts.note: lit means illuminated

indicators.note: erased means the courtyard word is wiped out of the artist's name

parts.note: a garth is a courtyard enclosed by cloisters

explanation.surface: A Hogarth etching of a cloistered courtyard rubbed out beside an illuminated manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogarth is the 18th-century English artist known for engraved prints.
explanation.definitionFit: A litho, short for lithograph, is a print made by lithography.
